3. The company invested $10 billion in Alphabet, $GOOGL, during Q2 in addition to acquiring Taylor Morrison Home for $6.8 billion

Berkshire Hathaway appears to be leaning bullish again.

candidates.text:
it’s now unclear to me that even openai realizes how strange the distinction between chat & work feels in practice & how fragmented the entire chatgpt experience has become.

like if you leave it on work, every simple question or search becomes an expedition. it starts thinking, planning, & using tools when you just wanted a quick answer.

if you leave it on chat, the product feels increasingly constrained & legacy. you often can’t choose the level of intelligence you want, & the moment you need it to actually do something, you have to switch back.

so there is no good default. chat is often too limited for real tasks. work is too slow & cumbersome for normal queries. constantly switching between them makes the entire product infinitely more complex.

also the lack of sync between mobile & desktop plus what’s a local chat vs cloud chat is a mess. chatgpt went from the most usable simple consumer experience to confusing af in such a short period of time. pretty nuts.

candidates.text:
I hate copy cats who're dishonest and copy others work blatantly and call it their own. Unfortunately, the design industry has a lot of them.

No amount of justification makes this right or safe. And I know controversies or callouts is not something what my followers here want to see from my profile... 

but I since my career has been standing on the shoulder of great designers, artists, engineers, thinkers, and good humans who got "inspired" but created something new out of it rather than copy-pasting and changing the title, keyword or the cover and call it their own.

Everyone on socials are pretty smart and they can call "inspired" from "stolen" pretty quickly and sharply.

If you're someone who's thiking of copying someone's work & calling it your won. DON'T. It's not worth your reputation.

Put in the reps. Think through the problem/output. Wait it out. A good inspiration will strike and then what you'll produce will really be outstanding and you'll be proud to call your own.

Reputation online >>>> stealing someone's work for a few likes.

candidates.text:
If you work in tech, you will want to read the ~40-page short novel Profession by Isaac Asimov, from 1957.

An unusually intelligent youngster decides they want to be a Registered Computer Programmer as demand for that profession is the highest of all. But he gets rejected... and even though the story was written 70 years ago, it's as if it described the world that could happen with AI, and who the most valuable people of such a world could be.

(thanks @ritakozlov for the recommendation!)
